title: Panoramic view of the WR 22 and Eta Carinae regions of the Carina Nebula
caption: The WR 22 and Eta Carinae regions of the Carina Nebula, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope
celestial: Carina Nebula, Eta Carinae, NGC 3372, WR 22 · constellation Carina · about 7500 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Ranked #32 on ESO’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: This wide panorama joins two views of the Carina Nebula. On the right is a newer image of the area around the Wolf–Rayet star WR 22. On the left is an earlier picture of the region around Eta Carinae, the star at the heart of the nebula, which the source describes as unique.

A Wolf–Rayet star is a very hot, massive star that is shedding its outer layers in a powerful wind. The nebula around both stars is a vast cloud of gas and dust about 7500 light-years away, in the constellation Carina.

Both images came from the Wide Field Imager, mounted on the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at ESO's La Silla Observatory in Chile, a camera suited to covering large areas of sky in one shot. The finished panorama is also sold as a mounted print in the ESOshop.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (57.84 x 28.17 arcminutes) and distance (7500 light years), the frame spans roughly 126 × 61 light-years. Its light set out about 7,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: The Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope observed the nebula in visible light through B, V and R filters. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: The camera's exposures gather far more light than the eye can.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

alt: A wide panorama of the Carina Nebula, joining the region around WR 22 on the right with the region around Eta Carinae on the left.
